verdicts.trueWording: drew the geography of the Six Duchies from Alaska
verdicts.note: Raw Guardian page, HTTP 200, browser UA. Reporter's narrative sentence in the paragraph after the Robin Hobb pen-name passage; page adds 'and the Pacific Northwest, where she and her husband lived for many years'. Byline Alison Flood confirmed. Paraphrase, not transcribed speech, as the routeHint says.

verdicts.trueWording: anything more than 250 pages long, 275 tops
verdicts.note: Raw page. Hobb's own speech, in the paragraph opening on fantasy being in a good place; framed by 'When I first started I was writing paperbacks, and I was told' and closed by the paperback-binding reason. Every limb on the page.

verdicts.trueWording: You set off events, and then you see coming into
verdicts.note: Raw page. Immediately follows Hobb's clockwork simile (shepherd and sheep striking a chime) applied to writing in a really big world; sentence completes 'view what they are triggering'. Sits in the Liveships/return-to-Fitz passage as the page hint says.

verdicts.trueWording: a respectable land-holder, a man of grapes and sheep now
verdicts.note: Raw Guardian page, fourth body paragraph, quoted from the novel and attributed 'he tells us, a little too firmly'. Preceded by 'I was no longer an assassin' and continued with ploughs and shears, not knives and swords, which carries the tools limb and the contrast with his former office.

Raw page, paragraph beginning that the novel isn't a quick starter. Continues '- years - of not much happening' and closes 'before events begin to spiral out of control', so both the months-and-years limb and the spiral limb are present.

verdicts.trueWording: the seeds of doom Hobb sowed so near the start
verdicts.note: Raw page, penultimate body paragraph. Continues 'of the novel finally begin to sprout', supplying the later-sprouting limb; the sentence goes on to Fitz's contentment starting to crumble.

verdicts.trueWording: that stone-dropping-into-a-well plunge of my heart
verdicts.note: Raw page, in the paragraph on the carving of Fitz, the Fool and the wolf Nighteyes; introduced by 'And there it was'. Grief context is the Fool's ten-year silence, so the concrete-figure-rather-than-abstraction limb holds.

verdicts.trueWording: the detail with which she depicts the Six Duchies world
verdicts.note: Raw Independent page, HTTP 200, third body paragraph (the review's middle). Sentence is 'Robin Hobb's secret is not just [this] ... but her emphasis on internal drama' - a two-part construction, and the first paragraph establishes the appeal to readers who usually avoid fantasy.

verdicts.trueWording: but her emphasis on internal drama
verdicts.note: Raw page, same sentence as index 483; it is the second half of the 'not just ... but' pair. Byline Amanda Craig, dated Friday 14 August 2015, consistent with the claim's year.

verdicts.trueWording: healing, clothing, kindness and the terror of rape are given
verdicts.note: Raw page, fourth body paragraph. Continues 'as much weight as combat, drinking, wealth and whoring'. The claim quotes a subset of each list, which the page supports; nothing in the claim is absent.

verdicts.trueWording: citizens are people who would rather trade and raise families
verdicts.note: Raw page, fifth body paragraph, opening 'The majority of its citizens ...' and closing 'than fight'. 'Its' refers back to the Six Duchies world of the preceding paragraph, supporting the Six Duchies limb.

verdicts.trueWording: you wish for more action and less introspection
verdicts.note: Raw page, fourth body paragraph, opening 'Indeed, by the time violence erupts into his life again'. Both the violence-erupts limb and the complaint limb are on the page; the sentence is a concession before the 'Yet this is' turn.

verdicts.trueWording: as familiar as those in a novel by Jonathan Franzen
verdicts.note: Raw page, third body paragraph as the claim states. Subject is 'the feelings of anguish, ambiguity, fear and failure', so the feelings limb is supported.

verdicts.trueWording: It is, without question, a slow novel
verdicts.note: Raw reactormag page, HTTP 200 on the canonical URL, byline 'By Justin Landon', published August 12, 2014. Sentence sits in the paragraph on the wide variance of impressions; 'without question' carries the claim's 'without qualification'.

verdicts.trueWording: Comparing it to more pastoral family dramas would be more appropriate
verdicts.note: Raw page, same paragraph as index 489, continuing 'than the action packed epic fantasies the previous Farseer books are often compared'. The article's own headline is 'Pastoral Family Drama'. The claim compresses the page's loose grammar but adds nothing the page lacks.
